intro: Compare the top AI video generation tools available in India in 2026. From Kling to Veo 3.1 and Seedance, find the best model for your content and budget.
takeaways: OpenAI shut down Sora in April 2026 - teams on the API must migrate before September 24, 2026
Google Veo 3.1 is the top general-purpose replacement with native audio, 4K, and flexible pricing
Kling AI leads for long-form narrative work; Runway Gen-4 for professional editing pipeline integration
Subscription costs start at $19.99/month; API pricing ranges from $0.24 to $4.80 per 8-second clip

body.text: Google Veo 3.1 is the strongest general-purpose choice for most Indian marketing teams in 2026, offering native audio generation, 4K output, and flexible API or subscription access, while Kling AI leads for long-form or character-consistent storytelling and Runway Gen-4 leads for teams that need tight integration into a professional editing pipeline. The choice matters more than usual right now because OpenAI's Sora, one of the category's early leaders, is shutting down entirely, forcing any team still using it to migrate before service ends.
Why Is This Decision Urgent Right Now

OpenAI announced on March 24, 2026 that it was discontinuing Sora less than six months after its public launch. The consumer app, including sora.com and the iOS and Android apps, closed on April 26, 2026. The developer API, covering the Sora 2 and Sora 2 Pro model endpoints, is scheduled to shut down on September 24, 2026, after which all associated user data will be permanently deleted (Cyberlink, April 2026; Apiyi, April 2026). Any Indian marketing team, agency, or developer with workflows, automations, or client deliverables built around the Sora API has a hard deadline to migrate before that date.

The shutdown was not framed as a sign that AI video demand is weak. Reporting pointed to Sora's inference costs, estimated at $8 to 12 million per month against revenue below $2 million, an active user base that dropped by more than half after initial launch hype faded, and the collapse of a reported $1 billion Disney partnership, with Disney said to have learned of the shutdown less than an hour before the public announcement (ZenCreator, April 2026; Cyberlink, April 2026). OpenAI has since redirected resources toward enterprise and coding-focused products rather than consumer video generation (ZenCreator, April 2026).

"The consensus across 2026 industry analysis is that switching is not just necessary because of the Sora shutdown, it is an upgrade regardless. Teams migrating now are moving toward tools that were already ahead on features Sora lacked."
What Should Replace Sora for a Marketing Team

Google's Veo 3.1 is the most commonly recommended direct replacement across 2026 industry comparisons, cited as matching or exceeding Sora's quality ceiling while adding native audio generation, which Sora never shipped, and offering both a generous free tier through Google AI products and predictable subscription or API-based pricing for teams with regular volume (Veo3ai.io, April 2026). For teams specifically prioritizing long-form storytelling or character consistency across multiple shots, Kling AI is frequently ranked ahead of Veo, with Kling 3.0 generating 4K video at 60fps with native audio and multi-shot subject-binding features aimed directly at the consistency problems that limited Sora (ZenCreator, April 2026). For studios and professional creative teams that need an editing-integrated workflow rather than a standalone generator, Runway Gen-4 is the recommended addition to a production stack, particularly for pipeline integration and multi-clip consistency (Veo3ai.io, April 2026).
What Does Veo 3.1 Actually Cost for a Marketing Team to Run Regularly

Pricing runs across three separate paths that a team needs to choose between rather than blend casually: a Google AI subscription for predictable monthly costs, developer API billing through Vertex AI or the Gemini API for programmatic or on-demand use, and a limited free tier for testing (Veo3ai.io, May 2026). On the subscription side, Google AI Pro runs at roughly $19.99 per month and includes enough credits for around 100 Lite-quality clips, 50 Fast-quality clips, or 10 full-quality clips through Google's Flow tool, while Google AI Ultra at roughly $249.99 per month scales that considerably higher for production teams generating video daily (CostGoat, 2026). On the API side, an eight-second clip runs from roughly $0.24 for 720p video-only output up to $4.80 for 4K output with audio, meaning cost scales directly with resolution and whether audio is included (DIYAI, 2026).
What Should an Indian Marketing or Agency Team Actually Do Before September 2026

Export and archive any existing Sora-generated assets before OpenAI's stated deletion timeline, since account data is permanently removed once the shutdown completes. Choose a primary replacement based on the team's dominant use case rather than trying to run parallel tools indefinitely: Veo 3.1 for general marketing and social content with audio needs, Kling for narrative or character-driven work, Runway for teams already embedded in a professional editing pipeline. Model the cost difference between subscription and API billing based on actual monthly volume, since API per-second pricing can be considerably cheaper for occasional use but more expensive than a flat subscription for high-frequency production. And build in review time for AI-generated video content against ASCI's evolving disclosure guidelines for AI-generated advertising material in India, since realistic AI-generated video used in ads is explicitly named as a medium-risk category requiring disclosure under ASCI's May 2026 draft guidelines.

Is Sora completely unavailable now, or is there still time to use it?
The consumer Sora app and website closed on April 26, 2026. The developer API remains available until September 24, 2026, after which it will be fully discontinued and all associated data permanently deleted. Any team still using the API needs to migrate before that date.

What is the best overall Sora replacement for a marketing team?
Google Veo 3.1 is the most commonly recommended general-purpose replacement in 2026 comparisons, offering native audio generation, up to 4K resolution, and both subscription and API pricing paths, making it suitable for most marketing use cases.

Which AI video tool is best for long, narrative-driven content?
Kling AI, particularly Kling 3.0, is frequently ranked ahead of alternatives for long-form storytelling and character consistency across multiple shots, addressing a limitation that affected Sora throughout its short lifespan.

How much does Veo 3.1 cost for regular business use?
Subscription pricing starts around $19.99 per month for Google AI Pro, which includes enough monthly credits for roughly 100 lower-quality clips or 10 full-quality clips. API pricing ranges from about $0.24 to $4.80 per eight-second clip depending on resolution and whether audio is included.

Why did OpenAI shut down Sora so quickly after launch?
Reported factors include unsustainable inference costs, estimated at $8 to 12 million per month against revenue under $2 million, a sharp drop in active users after initial launch interest faded, and the collapse of a major partnership, alongside OpenAI's broader strategic shift toward enterprise and coding-focused products.

Do AI-generated marketing videos need a disclosure label in India?
Under ASCI's Draft Guidelines for Responsible Labelling of AI-Generated Content in Advertising, published May 2026, realistic AI-generated video content used in advertising falls into a medium-risk category that requires a clear, prominent AI disclosure or the advertisement is considered misleading under ASCI's code.
